report_metadata.platform: Web3 Sentinel - Smart Contract Security Analysis

methodology.static_analysis: Slither static analysis framework + Sentinel Custom AST heuristic rules

findings.title: Reentrancy via Checks-Effects-Interactions Violation
findings.description: In function 'withdraw', an external low-level call sends Ether at line 28 before state variables are updated at line 32. A malicious receiver can recursively invoke this function before the state update occurs.
findings.impact: Complete drainage of contract funds through recursive external calls.
findings.reproduction:
1. Deploy an attacking contract with a receive() callback that calls the vulnerable function.
2. Deposit minimal funds.
3. Call the withdraw function to trigger recursive execution until contract balance reaches zero.
findings.remediation:
1. Apply the Checks-Effects-Interactions (CEI) pattern: update state variables before making external calls.
2. Inherit OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuard and decorate the function with `nonReentrant`.
